methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. mindtraced_atomic_units: The module `top_module` implements a 512-cell Rule 90 cellular automaton.
Rule 90 is a one-dimensional cellular automaton where the next state of each cell is the XOR of its two neighbors.
The module has a clock input `clk`.
The module has a load signal `load`.
The module has a 512-bit data input `data`.
The module has a 512-bit output `q` representing the current state of the cells.
The cells are indexed from 0 to 511 (q[511:0]).
When `load` is asserted, the cells are initialized with `data`.
When `load` is not asserted, on each rising edge of `clk`, the cells update their state according to Rule 90.
The boundary conditions are such that the neighbors of q[0] and q[511] are always 0.
The next state of q[0] is calculated as 0 XOR q[1].
The next state of q[511] is calculated as q[510] XOR 0.
spec_atomic_units: The module `top_module` implements a Rule 90 cellular automaton.
The module has a clock input `clk`.
The module has a load enable input `load`.
The module has a 512-bit data input `data`.
The module has a 512-bit output register `q`.
When `load` is asserted, the `data` input is loaded into the `q` register.
The `clk` signal is used for the sequential update of the `q` register based on the Rule 90 logic.
The next state of each cell is determined by the XOR of its left and right neighbors.
The boundary conditions are defined such that the neighbors of the leftmost and rightmost cells are considered to be 0.
When `load` is asserted, the output `q` is directly assigned the value of the input `data`.
When `load` is deasserted, the output `q` is updated with the result of the Rule 90 combinational logic (`next_q`).
The output `q` changes on the rising edge of `clk`.
When `load` is high, `q` is loaded with `data` on the rising edge of `clk`.
When `load` is low, `q` is updated with the Rule 90 calculation on the rising edge of `clk`.
The module contains a 512-bit register `q` declared as `output reg [511:0] q`.
The register `q` is updated inside an `always @(posedge clk)` block using non-blocking assignments (`<=`).
When `load` is asserted, `q` is assigned the value of `data`.

When `load` is not asserted, `q` is assigned the next state based on the Rule 90 calculation, where the next state of each cell is the XOR of its two neighbors, with boundary conditions q[-1] and q[512] equal to 0.
